title: Hail to the Future Leaders of Our Country
primary_topics: Closing address at the FLP 2021 Awards Ceremony (online due to COVID-19), August 13, 2021

Hailing and commissioning the FLP Scholars Society (FLPSS) as the network of future leaders of the country -- super lawyers, justices, legislators, governors, cabinet members, chief justices, and presidents
Accountability of scholars to the FLP bar topnotcher tradition: Borja (1st), Gaw (5th), Manuel (6th), Rojas (9th) -- 100% passing rate from the first two batches

Two ambitious new initiatives: (1) ESME/ESMEL fellowship expansion to MBA programs in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics and business law; (2) the Entrepreneurship Fund of about P1 billion for MSMEs
sub_topics: Thanks to CJ Gesmundo (Board of Judges chair; Scholarship Program) and SAJ Estela Perlas-Bernabe (Board of Judges chair; Dissertation Writing Contest; third time; to retire May next year but hoped to continue after retirement)

CJP's full concurrence with CJ Gesmundo's thesis: 'the power of the judiciary, far from being passive and weak is actually dynamic and compelling' and 'the power to resolve and decide issues and controversies with finality carries with it guidance on future actions'
Thanks to Secretary of Justice Menardo I. Guevarra: CJP looks forward every Sunday to his WhatsApp insights on the Inquirer column

Partners: Tan Yan Kee Foundation (Dr. Lucio C. Tan as Chairman, brother Harry C. Tan as Vice Chairman) for Scholarship Program; Ayala Corporation (Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala) for Dissertation Writing Contest
COVID-19 cancelled the November bar examination -- no new topnotchers at this ceremony; will give cash grants to future topnotchers from batches 3 and 4 at next year's ceremony

Bar topnotcher tradition: Sean James Borja (1st, batch 1); Katrina Gaw (5th, batch 1); Kenneth Glenn Manuel (6th, batch 2); Jun Dexter Rojas (9th, batch 2); 100% passing rate across all scholars who took the exam

FLPSS induction of present batch: exclusive group; membership limited to those who pass exacting qualifications; no hazing or corporal punishment -- just academic excellence and commitment to liberty-and-prosperity philosophy
FLPSS as future leaders: in 10-20 years, scholars will be super lawyers, justices, judges, legislators, governors, mayors, cabinet members, chief justices, and presidents

Invitation to intimate sessions at CJP's home in small batches of 10-12 -- idea inspired by 'Tuesdays with Morrie' (Mitch Albom); 'Sundays with Jovy' account: Salonga used to visit CJP at home after both retired to exchange ideas -- insisted on coming to CJP's home after considering CJP his mentor after CJP became Salonga's chief legal counsel when Salonga was Senate President

ESME expansion: scholarships and dissertation writing contests for post-graduate students in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management and economics (ESME); proposed to AIM to create new programs in ESME fields; FLPSS members can apply

Entrepreneurship Fund of about P1 billion: to help manage and invest equity in small and medium enterprises with social impact but no bank access -- the 'smallness' and lack of expertise/capital problem; discussed with FLP trustees

Caveat to FLPSS: do not create unnecessary division and chaos within the Society; may participate in partisan politics externally but not within the Society; 'minds are like parachutes -- they work only when they are open'; inside the Society: united in common pursuit

Closing promise: 'Though I may be already in the Great Beyond, my spirit will be hovering above you, beside you and behind you -- humbly to inspire and guide you in your journey of life, liberty and livelihood for our people and for our country'

stances.claim: The FLP Scholars Society's members are destined to be the future leaders of the country -- super lawyers, justices, judges, legislators, governors, mayors, cabinet members, chief justices, and presidents -- in 10 to 20 years. The FLP's investment in them is an investment in the Philippines' next governing generation.
stances.rhetorical_move: prophetic-commissioning: naming the future roles explicitly as a motivational frame for present scholars
stances.confidence: asserted as aspiration with institutional backing (100% passing rate on bar, multiple topnotchers)

stances.claim: The 100% passing rate and four bar topnotchers from the first two FLP scholar batches (Borja 1st, Gaw 5th, Manuel 6th, Rojas 9th) is not an accident but the standard. The third and fourth batches must 'rise to the level of excellence set by your predecessors.'
stances.rhetorical_move: tradition-as-obligation: the track record as a normative benchmark that creates a duty of performance

stances.claim: Within the FLPSS, unity around the philosophy of liberty, prosperity and the rule of law must be maintained -- there are no political, ideological, social, religious, gender or medical issues that can deflect the Society from its common vision. Members may participate in partisan politics externally but not within the Society.
stances.rhetorical_move: internal-unity mandate with external-freedom concession: the Society as a protected non-partisan space

notable_anecdotes: 'Sundays with Jovy': after both retired, Salonga used to visit CJP at home to exchange ideas on current events and on CJP's Inquirer columns. CJP pleaded that the younger and less-endowed one should be the visitor, but Salonga insisted on coming to CJP's home because 'he already considered me his mentor after I became his chief legal counsel when he was president of the Senate.' CJP calls this his 'Sundays with Jovy -- ala Mitch Albom.'

The intimate-sessions idea: CJP proposes inviting FLP scholars in small batches of 10-12 to his home for intimate exchanges on how to advance liberty and prosperity in their schools, families and communities -- modeled on 'Tuesdays with Morrie' by Mitch Albom.

Bar topnotcher roll: Sean James Borja (1st, batch 1), Katrina Gaw (5th, batch 1), Kenneth Glenn Manuel (6th, batch 2), Jun Dexter Rojas (9th, batch 2). '100 percent of them, successfully hurdled the tests.'

The haunting promise: 'Though I may be already in the Great Beyond, my spirit will be hovering above you, beside you and behind you -- humbly to inspire and guide you in your journey of life, liberty and livelihood for our people and for our country.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered August 13, 2021 at FLP's online Awards Ceremony, this closing address by CJP thanks CJ Gesmundo (Scholarship Board of Judges chair), SAJ Perlas-Bernabe (Dissertation Board of Judges chair, third time; hoped to continue after her May 2022 retirement), Secretary of Justice Guevarra (whose Sunday WhatsApp insights on CJP's Inquirer columns are eagerly anticipated), and partners Tan Yan Kee Foundation (Dr. Lucio Tan as Chairman, Harry Tan as Vice Chairman) and Ayala Corporation (Jaime Augusto Zobel). He acknowledges that the COVID-19 pandemic cancelled the November bar exam -- so there are no new topnotchers at this ceremony -- but cites the bar-topnotcher tradition from the first two FLP batches: Sean James Borja (1st), Katrina Gaw (5th), Kenneth Glenn Manuel (6th), and Jun Dexter Rojas (9th), with a 100% passing rate. He hails the FLP Scholars Society members as destined to be 'in 10 or 20 years... the super lawyers, the justices and judges, the legislators, the governors and mayors, the cabinet members, the chief justices, and the presidents who will shape our destiny.' He introduces the intimate-sessions idea (small batches of 10-12 at his home, modeled on 'Tuesdays with Morrie'), recalling 'Sundays with Jovy' -- Salonga's insistence on visiting CJP at home after CJP became Salonga's chief legal counsel during his Senate presidency. He announces two new initiatives: the ESME fellowship expansion (MBA scholarships in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics, and business law, with an AIM curriculum proposal) and the Entrepreneurship Fund of about P1 billion for MSMEs with social impact but no bank access. He closes with an internal-unity caveat (no partisan activities within the Society; 'minds are like parachutes -- they work only when they are open') and a haunting farewell promise: 'Though I may be already in the Great Beyond, my spirit will be hovering above you, beside you and behind you.'
